body_text:
The inclusion $\mathbb{Z}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{Q}$ identifies $a$
with $a/1$. If $F$ is any field and $\varphi:\mathbb{Z}\to F$ is
an injective ring homomorphism, there is a unique field
homomorphism $\widetilde\varphi:\mathbb{Q}\to F$ satisfying
$\widetilde\varphi(a/b)=\varphi(a)\varphi(b)^{-1}$. This is the
universal property of the fraction field.
